name: KDIGO 2024 CKD Evaluation & Management
keys: Risk stratification by eGFRcr-cys + ACR; RASi + SGLT2i + finerenone backbone for proteinuric CKD (DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY, FIDELIO/FIGARO). GLP-1 RA per FLOW (semaglutide, 24% kidney composite reduction). KFRE for individualized progression risk; SGLT2i now indicated at eGFR >=20.

name: KDIGO 2024 Blood Pressure in CKD
keys: Target SBP <120 (SPRINT-informed) when tolerated; do not stop RASi for modest eGFR bumps or mild hyperkalemia. Recommendation primarily CV-driven, not kidney-outcome driven.

name: KDIGO 2022 Diabetes in CKD
keys: SGLT2i first-line for T2DM + CKD regardless of A1c (eGFR >=20). Metformin if eGFR >=30. GLP-1 RA layered for additional glycemic / weight control. Decouple glycemic control from kidney protection.

name: KDIGO 2021 Glomerulonephritis
keys: ANCA vasculitis: rituximab (RAVE) or cyclophosphamide + reduced steroids (PEXIVAS); avacopan as steroid-sparing C5a inhibitor. Lupus nephritis: induction with belimumab + MMF or voclosporin (AURORA-1); membranous: rituximab if anti-PLA2R+ (MENTOR). IgA: sparsentan (PROTECT).

name: KDIGO 2024 CKD-MBD update
keys: Dietary phosphate first; non-calcium phosphate binders preferred. Vitamin D analogs and calcimimetics for severe SHPT. PTH targets a range (2-9x ULN) in dialysis. Aluminum binders historic / avoid.

name: KDIGO 2012 AKI (2026 update in review)
keys: Three-bucket etiology (prerenal/intrinsic/postrenal) drives action. Hold nephrotoxins; optimize perfusion. RRT for refractory hyperkalemia/acidosis, volume overload, uremic complications, dialyzable toxins. AKIKI / STARRT-AKI: no benefit from accelerated RRT timing.

name: KDIGO 2025 ADPKD
keys: Tolvaptan slows kidney volume increase (TEMPO 3:4) and preserves eGFR in rapid-progressors. Liver enzyme monitoring required. Genetic testing helpful for prognosis and family screening.

name: AUA 2023 BPH Guideline
keys: IPSS-driven evaluation. Alpha-blockers and 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors first-line; combination if both LUTS and large prostate. Surgical options including PVP, WVTT, laser enucleation, PAE.

name: 2025 AHA/ACC Hypertension (Renal Lens)
keys: Target <130/80 for most adults; resistant HTN -> spironolactone (PATHWAY-2 demonstrated mineralocorticoid excess physiology). Expanded primary aldosteronism screening for stage 2 / resistant HTN. PREVENT calculator replaces pooled cohort equations.

name: 2025 AHA/ACC Hypertension Guideline
keys: Target BP <130/80 for most adults. PREVENT replaces pooled cohort equations. Expanded aldosteronism screening for stage 2 and resistant HTN. Renal denervation as adjunct for resistant HTN. SPRINT-era data drove targets down for stroke and HF prevention.

name: 2023 ACC/AHA/ACCP/HRS Atrial Fibrillation
keys: Two separable questions: stroke risk (CHA2DS2-VASc -> DOAC > warfarin per ARISTOTLE/RE-LY/ROCKET-AF) and rhythm management. EAST-AFNET 4 supports early rhythm control; CASTLE-AF / CABANA support ablation in symptomatic AF + HFrEF.

name: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Heart Failure
keys: HFrEF four-pillar GDMT started together: ARNi (PARADIGM-HF) > ACEi/ARB; beta-blocker; MRA; SGLT2i (DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced). HFpEF: SGLT2i Class 2a (EMPEROR-Preserved, DELIVER). IV iron for iron-deficient (AFFIRM-AHF). ICD/CRT per EF + QRS.

name: 2025 ACC/AHA ACS
keys: Unified STEMI/NSTEMI framework (plaque instability spectrum). Early invasive for high-risk NSTEMI. Ticagrelor/prasugrel preferred over clopidogrel post-PCI (PLATO, TRITON-TIMI 38). Radial access (RIVAL, MATRIX). DAPT individualized; colchicine (COLCOT, LoDoCo2) as anti-inflammatory secondary prevention.

name: 2020 ACC/AHA Valvular Heart Disease
keys: TAVR across all risk tiers (PARTNER 1/2/3, CoreValve). MitraClip for severe functional MR with HF (COAPT). Multidisciplinary heart team evaluation required. Endocarditis prophylaxis for high-risk native/prosthetic valves only.

name: 2025 ESC Myocarditis & Pericarditis
keys: Myopericarditis: viral/autoimmune myocardial inflammation. NSAIDs or colchicine first-line; corticosteroids second-line (recurrence risk). Anakinra/rilonacept for autoimmune/giant-cell forms. CMR-PET-FDG imaging guidance.

name: 2026 ACC/AHA Dyslipidemia
keys: LDL is causal for atherosclerosis: lower is better in high-risk. High-intensity statin first; ezetimibe (15-20% LDL); PCSK9i (FOURIER, ODYSSEY: 40-60% LDL); bempedoic acid (CLEAR Outcomes) for statin-intolerant. LDL <55 for very high-risk ASCVD. Lp(a) measured once.

name: 2017 ACC/AHA/HRS Syncope
keys: TLOC from cerebral hypoperfusion: vasovagal, orthostatic, cardiac arrhythmia, structural. History/exam + 12-lead ECG Class 1 (find QT prolongation, Brugada, ARVC). Routine labs/imaging not useful; EP/ICD only if structural/arrhythmic suspected.

name: 2023 Duke-ISCVID Endocarditis Criteria
keys: IE = bacterial valve seeding from bacteremia/dental/IVDU causing vegetation + emboli. Updated 2023 criteria add PCR, metagenomic sequencing, FDG-PET/CT. Sensitivity 84% (vs 75% for modified Duke 2000). Empiric ceftriaxone + vancomycin; POET supports IV-to-PO switch.

name: 2022 ACC/AHA Aortic Disease
keys: Medial degeneration drives dissection/aneurysm in HTN + connective tissue disease. Surgical threshold reduced to 5.0 cm at expert centers. Growth >=0.3 cm/yr over 2y or >=0.5 cm/yr triggers repair. Beta-blockers / ARBs lower aortic stress.

name: 2024 AHA/ACC HCM
keys: Sarcomeric mutations cause LVH, diastolic dysfunction, LVOT obstruction; SCD risk. Genetic testing + CMR risk stratification; ICD for SCD prevention. Disopyramide / verapamil for symptoms; mavacamten (cardiac myosin inhibitor) reduces LVOT gradient (EXPLORER-HCM).

name: 2023 AHA/ACC Chronic Coronary Disease
keys: Stable atherosclerotic plaque with progressive ischemia. Stress imaging guides management. DAPT >=6 months post-DES (prasugrel/ticagrelor). Beta-blockers, CCBs, or ranolazine for symptoms. ACEi/ARB + statin in all per HOPE/LIPID/HPS.

name: 2021 ACC/AHA/SCAI Coronary Revascularization
keys: Heart Team for complex multivessel/left main disease. FFR/iFR <=0.80/<=0.89 guides PCI of intermediate lesions (FAME, FAME 2). STEMI with multivessel disease: complete revascularization during index hospitalization (COMPLETE, FULL REVASC) reduces MI/death. Diabetes + multivessel CAD: CABG preferred over PCI (FREEDOM, BARI 2D). Radial access default (RIVAL, MATRIX). Left main: CABG Class 1; PCI reasonable for low/intermediate SYNTAX (EXCEL, NOBLE caveats).

name: 2024 ACC/AHA Multisociety Lower Extremity PAD
keys: ABI <=0.90 diagnoses PAD; toe-brachial if non-compressible. Structured/supervised exercise therapy first-line for claudication, superior to revascularization for walking distance. Statin + antiplatelet (aspirin or clopidogrel per CAPRIE) for all symptomatic PAD. Low-dose rivaroxaban 2.5mg BID + aspirin reduces MALE/MACE (COMPASS, VOYAGER PAD post-revasc). CLTI: multidisciplinary limb team; endovascular vs surgical bypass per anatomy (BEST-CLI: vein bypass superior with adequate GSV).

name: 2026 AHA/ACC Acute Pulmonary Embolism (US) + ESC 2019
keys: The 2026 AHA/ACC (with ACCP, ACEP, CHEST, SCAI, SHM, SIR, SVM, SVN) guideline is the FIRST dedicated US PE guideline and is now the US reference. MAJOR CHANGE: it introduces ACUTE PE CLINICAL CATEGORIES A through E with subcategories and RETIRES the massive / submassive vocabulary. ESC 2019 has NOT been re-issued and remains ESC current, using the parallel strata low / intermediate-low / intermediate-high / high - say which taxonomy you are teaching. Management: risk-stratify by hemodynamics, sPESI, RV dysfunction (echo or CT), troponin. High-risk (shock or arrest): systemic thrombolysis (alteplase 100mg over 2h; PEITHO-informed bleeding risk); catheter-directed therapy or surgical embolectomy if lysis is contraindicated. Intermediate-high: monitor 48-72h with rescue lysis on decompensation; catheter-directed thrombolysis evolving (ULTIMA, PE-TRACT). Low-risk (sPESI 0): outpatient DOAC (HoT-PE). Apixaban and rivaroxaban are single-drug regimens; dabigatran and edoxaban need a parenteral lead-in. YEARS algorithm adapts D-dimer cut-off to pretest probability. Anticoagulate at least 3 months.

name: GOLD 2025 COPD Strategy
keys: ABE assessment groups (replaces ABCD). Triple ICS-LABA-LAMA preferred for exacerbators (IMPACT, ETHOS); ensifentrine (PDE3/4 inhibitor) for persistent dyspnea. Anthonisen criteria for exacerbation antibiotics. NIV first-line for hypercapnic respiratory failure. LTOT if SpO2 <=88% (NOTT/MRC).

name: GINA 2025 Asthma
keys: Track 1 (preferred): as-needed ICS-formoterol (SMART/MART). Track 2: SABA + separate ICS. Type-2 biologics for severe: omalizumab (IgE), mepolizumab/reslizumab/benralizumab (IL-5), dupilumab (IL-4Ra), tezepelumab (TSLP).

name: ATS 2022 IPF / Progressive PF
keys: Nintedanib (TKI: PDGFR/FGFR/VEGFR) reduces FVC decline 125 mL/yr (INPULSIS); pirfenidone modulates TGF-beta (CAPACITY/ASCEND). Both for IPF and progressive non-IPF PPF. Lung transplant referral early for advanced disease.

name: 2022 ESC/ERS Pulmonary Hypertension
keys: PH redefined as mPAP >20 mmHg. Three-step diagnostic: clinical suspicion -> echo -> RHC confirmation. Risk-based management; initial combination therapy (ERA + PDE5i + sotatercept-emerging) per AMBITION/STELLAR. PEA / BPA for CTEPH.

name: 2026 AHA/ACC Acute Pulmonary Embolism (US) + ESC 2019
keys: The 2026 AHA/ACC (with ACCP, ACEP, CHEST, SCAI, SHM, SIR, SVM, SVN) guideline is the FIRST dedicated US PE guideline and is now the US reference. MAJOR CHANGE: it introduces ACUTE PE CLINICAL CATEGORIES A through E with subcategories and RETIRES the massive / submassive vocabulary. ESC 2019 has NOT been re-issued and remains ESC current, using the parallel strata low / intermediate-low / intermediate-high / high - say which taxonomy you are teaching. Management: risk-stratify by hemodynamics, sPESI, RV dysfunction (echo or CT), troponin. High-risk (shock or arrest): systemic thrombolysis (alteplase 100mg over 2h; PEITHO-informed bleeding risk); catheter-directed therapy or surgical embolectomy if lysis is contraindicated. Intermediate-high: monitor 48-72h with rescue lysis on decompensation; catheter-directed thrombolysis evolving (ULTIMA, PE-TRACT). Low-risk (sPESI 0): outpatient DOAC (HoT-PE). Apixaban and rivaroxaban are single-drug regimens; dabigatran and edoxaban need a parenteral lead-in. YEARS algorithm adapts D-dimer cut-off to pretest probability. Anticoagulate at least 3 months.

name: 2023 BTS Pleural Disease
keys: Pneumothorax: symptom-based (not size-based) management; conservative or ambulatory options. Pleural infection: TPA + DNAse intrapleural (MIST2) for empyema. MPE: indwelling pleural catheter or talc pleurodesis.

name: ATS 2025 CAP (IDSA did not endorse)
keys: CONTESTED - there is no longer a single consensus. ATS published a 2025 CAP update; IDSA DECLINED TO ENDORSE it (IDSA accepted 8 of 10 recommendations but rejected the 2 concerning antibiotics in patients with positive viral assays). Teach the split. ATS 2025 changes vs IDSA/ATS 2019: (1) CORTICOSTEROIDS now suggested in SEVERE CAP (conditional, low-quality evidence) EXCEPT influenza pneumonia - a REVERSAL of 2019 which recommended against routine steroids; this is the highest-yield change. (2) SHORTER DURATION - 3 to 5 days conditionally recommended for outpatients with comorbidities and inpatients with non-severe CAP who reach clinical stability (minimum 3 days), down from at least 5 days. (3) Lung ultrasound addressed as a diagnostic modality. UNCHANGED from 2019: HCAP category eliminated, assess individual MRSA/Pseudomonas risk, CURB-65 and ATS minor criteria for site-of-care, outpatient amoxicillin or doxycycline (macrolide only if local resistance is low), inpatient beta-lactam + macrolide or respiratory fluoroquinolone.

name: 2024 ATS/CDC/ERS/IDSA TB Treatment
keys: 4-month RIPM (rifapentine/isoniazid/pyrazinamide/moxifloxacin) for drug-susceptible (Study 31, non-inferior to 6-month standard). 6-month BPaLM for RIF-resistant. LTBI: 3HP weekly x12w or 4R.

name: 2023 ATS/ESICM/SCCM ARDS
keys: Low TV 4-8 mL/kg PBW. Prone position >=16 h/day for moderate-severe (PROSEVA, NNT 6). Neuromuscular blockade for refractory hypoxemia. Conservative fluid; ECMO referral early for refractory.

name: AASM OSA 2024
keys: Inpatient OSA screening in high-risk hospitalized. PAP first-line for moderate-severe. Surgical / oral appliance for select patients. Hypoglossal nerve stimulation (Inspire) for moderate OSA failing CPAP.

name: Fleischner 2017 Pulmonary Nodules
keys: Risk-based follow-up <3 cm. <6 mm: low risk no f/u; 6-8 mm: 6-12 mo CT; >8 mm: 3 mo CT or PET. Subsolid nodules: longer follow-up (5 years).

name: ATS/ERS Bronchiectasis 2024
keys: Airway clearance cornerstone. Long-term macrolide for >=2 exacerbations/yr (BAT, EMBRACE). Against chronic ICS unless coexistent COPD/asthma. Inhaled mannitol/hypertonic saline mucolytic options.

name: AASM OSA Diagnostic Testing 2017 (reaffirmed 2024)
keys: Screen high-risk adults with STOP-BANG or Berlin. In-lab PSG gold standard; home sleep apnea testing (HSAT) acceptable only for uncomplicated high pretest probability moderate-severe OSA — repeat with PSG if HSAT negative/inadequate. Avoid HSAT if cardiopulmonary disease, neuromuscular disease, opioid use, or non-OSA sleep disorder suspected. CPAP first-line; mandibular advancement device for mild-moderate or CPAP-intolerant; hypoglossal nerve stimulator (Inspire, STAR) for AHI 15-65 with BMI<32 and non-concentric collapse.

name: CHEST/ACCP Antithrombotic Therapy for VTE 2021
keys: DOACs (apixaban, rivaroxaban, edoxaban, dabigatran) preferred over warfarin for acute VTE (AMPLIFY, EINSTEIN, RE-COVER, Hokusai). Exceptions favoring warfarin/LMWH: CrCl<30, triple-positive APLS (TRAPS), mechanical valves. Cancer-VTE: apixaban or edoxaban preferred (CARAVAGGIO, Hokusai-Cancer); avoid edoxaban/rivaroxaban with luminal GI tumors. Provoked: 3 months. Unprovoked or persistent factor: indefinite low-dose apixaban 2.5mg BID or rivaroxaban 10mg daily (AMPLIFY-EXT, EINSTEIN-CHOICE).

name: ESC/ERS Pulmonary Hypertension 2022
keys: Hemodynamic definition revised: mPAP >20 mmHg (was ≥25). PAH (Group 1): PAWP <=15 + PVR >2 WU on right heart cath — mandatory. WSPH classification: I PAH, II left heart, III lung/hypoxia, IV CTEPH, V multifactorial. Initial dual oral therapy (ERA + PDE5i: ambrisentan-tadalafil per AMBITION) for low/intermediate risk; add selexipag (GRIPHON), macitentan (MERIT). Parenteral prostacyclin (epoprostenol, treprostinil) for high-risk. CTEPH: pulmonary endarterectomy first-line; riociguat if inoperable.

name: ATS ARDS Management Update 2024
keys: Berlin: acute hypoxemia within 7d, bilateral infiltrates, not fully explained by cardiac failure. Severity by P/F on PEEP >=5: mild 200-300, mod 100-200, severe <100. Low tidal volume 4-8 mL/kg PBW, plateau <30 cm H2O (ARMA). Higher PEEP for moderate-severe (ALVEOLI, LOVS). Prone positioning >=16h/day for P/F<150 (PROSEVA — 50% mortality reduction). NMB (cisatracurium) short-term in severe (ACURASYS; ROSE neutral). VV-ECMO for refractory P/F<80 (EOLIA, CESAR). Steroids suggested (DEXA-ARDS).

name: ACG GERD 2022
keys: Empiric PPI 8-week trial for typical GERD. Endoscopy for alarm symptoms (dysphagia, weight loss, GI bleed) and Barrett risk factors. Long-term PPI risks (CKD, fractures) overstated; continue if symptoms recur.

name: ACG Eosinophilic Esophagitis 2025
keys: >=15 eos/hpf diagnostic. Shared decision: 1-FED/2-FED elimination diet, topical steroids (fluticasone/budesonide), or dupilumab (LIBERTY-EoE). Maintenance therapy required to prevent fibrostenosis.

name: ACG H. pylori Treatment 2024
keys: Bismuth quadruple therapy (BQT) 14 days preferred for treatment-naive due to clarithromycin resistance. Vonoprazan-based therapy emerging. Test of cure >=4 weeks post-treatment.

name: ACG Celiac Disease 2023
keys: EGD with multiple duodenal biopsies for confirmation. High-titer TTG IgA >10x ULN + positive EMA can avoid biopsy in select cases. Lifelong gluten-free diet; pneumococcal vaccination per asplenia risk.

name: AGA Crohn Disease 2020
keys: Top-down advanced therapy (anti-TNF, ustekinumab, risankizumab/mirikizumab anti-IL23, vedolizumab) over step-up for moderate-severe. Combination anti-TNF + thiopurine reduces immunogenicity. Upadacitinib JAKi as alternative.

name: USPSTF Colorectal Cancer Screening 2021
keys: Lowered start age 50 -> 45 (rising young-onset CRC). Options: colonoscopy q10y, FIT annually, sDNA-FIT q3y, flexible sigmoidoscopy. Individualized 76-85. Stop after 85.

name: ACG IBS 2021
keys: Positive diagnostic strategy (Rome IV) over diagnosis of exclusion. Low-FODMAP diet for symptom relief. IBS-D: rifaximin, eluxadoline. IBS-C: linaclotide, plecanatide, lubiprostone. Gut-directed psychotherapy.

name: ACG C. difficile 2021
keys: Fidaxomicin first-line for initial CDI (lower recurrence vs vancomycin). Vancomycin 125 mg PO QID x 10d alternative. FMT for recurrent CDI (>=2 recurrences). Bezlotoxumab for prevention in high-risk.

name: ACG Acute Pancreatitis 2024
keys: Early oral feeding within 24-48h for mild AP. Enteral nutrition prevents infection in moderate-severe. Lactated Ringer's preferred over normal saline (WATERFALL). Delay intervention 4+ weeks for walled-off necrosis.

name: AASLD HCV 2023 (living document)
keys: Universal screening recommended. Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir or sofosbuvir/velpatasvir 8-12 weeks pangenotypic; >95% SVR. Simplified treatment for treatment-naive non-cirrhotic. Pediatric treatment >=3 years.

name: AASLD Cirrhosis & Ascites 2021/2024
keys: Variceal bleed: octreotide + ceftriaxone (SBP prophylaxis) + EVL. Ascites: spironolactone + furosemide; refractory -> TIPS or LVP + albumin. HRS-AKI: terlipressin + albumin (CONFIRM, 36% reversal vs placebo). HE: lactulose +/- rifaximin.

name: AASLD MASLD 2024
keys: Renamed from NAFLD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease). Lifestyle (5-10% weight loss) + comorbidity management; SGLT2i / GLP-1 RA for diabetes/obesity. Resmetirom (THR-beta agonist) FDA-approved for noncirrhotic MASH F2-F3 (MAESTRO-NASH).

name: AASLD/IDSA Chronic Hepatitis B 2025
keys: 2025 GRADE-based guideline REPLACES AASLD 2018. IMMUNE-TOLERANT PHASE: treat if age over 40, or grade 2 or higher inflammation / stage F2 or higher fibrosis (2018 largely deferred treatment here); shared decision-making under 40. DISCONTINUATION: in HBeAg-negative non-cirrhotic patients with sustained undetectable DNA, do NOT withdraw nucleos(t)ide analogue therapy until HBsAg loss - firmer than the 2018 finite-therapy option. PMTCT: strong recommendation for TDF or TAF at gestational week 28 when HBV DNA is over 200,000 IU/mL, regardless of HBeAg status. Tenofovir and entecavir remain first-line. Baseline treat thresholds: HBeAg-positive with DNA over 20,000 and ALT over 2x ULN; HBeAg-negative with DNA over 2,000 and elevated ALT. New guidance on the indeterminate or grey-zone phase and on HCC surveillance. Universal screening (HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HBc) per CDC 2023.

name: AGA 2024 Moderate-Severe Ulcerative Colitis
keys: Early advanced therapy over step-up. Higher-efficacy options for biologic-naive: infliximab, vedolizumab, upadacitinib, risankizumab, guselkumab, ozanimod (S1P modulator). Anti-TNF (infliximab + thiopurine combo per UC-SUCCESS), anti-integrin vedolizumab (GEMINI), anti-IL12/23 ustekinumab (UNIFI), JAKi tofacitinib/upadacitinib (OCTAVE, U-ACHIEVE). Steroid-sparing essential; confirm active inflammation by biomarkers/endoscopy before escalation. Mild-moderate: oral + topical 5-ASA (mesalamine).

name: AGA 2025 Moderate-Severe Crohn's Disease
keys: Biologic-naive: higher-efficacy first — infliximab + immunomodulator combo (SONIC), adalimumab, ustekinumab (UNITI), risankizumab (ADVANCE/MOTIVATE), guselkumab, mirikizumab; vedolizumab gut-selective option. Previously exposed: adalimumab, risankizumab, guselkumab, or upadacitinib (U-EXCEL/U-EXCEED) preferred; ustekinumab/mirikizumab intermediate. Treat-to-target with mucosal/endoscopic healing (STRIDE-II, CALM). Avoid prolonged steroids. Certolizumab pegol and vedolizumab lower efficacy in pretreated.

name: ADA Standards of Care 2025
keys: Metformin baseline + early combination. SGLT2i for ASCVD/HF/CKD regardless of A1c (EMPA-REG, CANVAS, DAPA-HF). GLP-1 RA for ASCVD/obesity (LEADER, REWIND, SUSTAIN-6, SELECT). Tirzepatide for weight loss (SURMOUNT). CGM for non-insulin T2DM.

name: Endocrine Society Hypopituitarism 2016
keys: 8-9am cortisol <3 = adrenal insufficiency; 3-15 ambiguous (cosyntropin stim or insulin tolerance test). Hydrocortisone 15-25 mg/day in divided doses; stress dosing for illness/surgery. Levothyroxine, sex hormones, GH per deficiency.

name: Endocrine Society Cushing 2015
keys: Screening: 24h urine free cortisol, late-night salivary cortisol, or 1-mg dexamethasone suppression. Treatment: transsphenoidal selective adenomectomy first-line (Cushing disease); unilateral adrenalectomy for adrenal adenoma. Ketoconazole/metyrapone/osilodrostat second-line.

name: Endocrine Society Primary Aldosteronism 2025
keys: 2025 guideline REPLACES 2016 and changes practice substantially. SCREEN ALL PATIENTS WITH HYPERTENSION (aldosterone + renin + ARR) - no longer restricted to resistant HTN / hypokalemia / incidentaloma / OSA / family history. CONFIRMATORY TESTING IS NO LONGER MANDATORY: diagnosis may rest on the biochemical triad of suppressed renin + elevated aldosterone + elevated ARR (saline infusion / oral salt loading no longer required in all cases). Measured PA prevalence among hypertensives rises from about 9 percent under 2016 criteria to about 16 percent under 2025 criteria, capturing milder phenotypes. Adrenal vein sampling still used when surgery is considered; lateralized disease -> adrenalectomy, bilateral -> mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist (spironolactone or eplerenone).

name: ATA Thyroid Nodules 2015 (nodule guidance still ATA current) + ATA DTC 2025
keys: NODULES - this 2015 guidance is STILL ATA CURRENT: ATA split the document, and the 2025 guideline covers DIFFERENTIATED THYROID CANCER only and explicitly EXCLUDES nodules (a separate nodule guideline is planned but not yet published). Nodule workup: ultrasound risk stratification (TI-RADS-like): high suspicion -> FNA at 1cm or more; intermediate -> 1-1.5cm; low -> 1.5cm; very low -> 2cm. Bethesda categories for FNA cytology; molecular testing for indeterminate nodules. THYROID CANCER - use ATA 2025 (Thyroid 2025;35:841), which is a major DE-ESCALATION: new COMPLETE REMISSION concept - low-risk DTC treated with total thyroidectomy plus RAI and a sustained excellent response for 10 to 15 years no longer needs routine biochemical surveillance (previously indefinite); further movement toward ACTIVE SURVEILLANCE over upfront surgery for papillary microcarcinoma; revised dynamic risk stratification plus new molecular and survivorship sections.

name: AACE/ATA Hypothyroidism 2014/2024
keys: TSH screening; treat if TSH >10 or symptoms with TSH 4.5-10. Levothyroxine 1.6 mcg/kg/day; titrate by TSH. Liothyronine combination not routinely recommended. Subclinical hypothyroidism treatment individualized.

name: AACE Postmenopausal Osteoporosis 2020
keys: T-score <=-2.5 diagnostic. First-line: alendronate, risedronate, zoledronate, denosumab. Anabolics (teriparatide, abaloparatide, romosozumab) for very-high-risk. FRAX >=20% major or 3% hip fracture risk treatment threshold.

name: KDIGO 2022 Diabetes in CKD
keys: SGLT2i for T2DM + CKD regardless A1c (eGFR >=20). Metformin if eGFR >=30. GLP-1 RA semaglutide for kidney protection (FLOW). Finerenone if eGFR >25, K normal, ACR >30 (FIDELIO/FIGARO).

name: AACE/ACE Postmenopausal Osteoporosis 2020
keys: Dx: T-score <=-2.5, fragility fracture, or FRAX >=20% major / >=3% hip. High risk: alendronate, risedronate, zoledronate, or denosumab first-line. Very high risk (T<=-3.0, recent fracture, multiple fx): anabolic first — romosozumab x12mo (ARCH vs alendronate), teriparatide or abaloparatide x2y (VERO, ACTIVE) — then sequence to antiresorptive. Denosumab 60mg SC q6mo — never stop without bisphosphonate follow-on (rebound vertebral fx). Bisphosphonate drug holiday after 3-5y IV / 5y oral if low risk.

name: ATA Hyperthyroidism & Thyrotoxicosis 2016
keys: Graves dx: suppressed TSH + elevated FT4/T3 + TRAb or diffuse RAIU. Three definitive options: methimazole 12-18mo (preferred initial; PTU only 1st-trimester pregnancy or storm due to hepatotoxicity), RAI ablation, or thyroidectomy. Beta-blocker for symptoms (propranolol, atenolol). Storm: PTU + iodine (Lugol/SSKI 1h after PTU) + hydrocortisone + beta-blocker + cooling. Moderate-severe orbitopathy: IV methylprednisolone pulse; teprotumumab (IGF-1R mAb) reduces proptosis per OPTIC (83% vs 10%).

name: ATA Hypothyroidism Treatment 2014
keys: Levothyroxine monotherapy standard: 1.6 mcg/kg/day overt; 25-75 mcg start subclinical. Take fasting, separate from calcium/iron/PPI by 4h. Recheck TSH q6-8wk after dose change; target mid-reference range (0.4-4.0). Treat subclinical if TSH >10, or 4.5-10 with symptoms, positive TPO, pregnancy, or CV risk. Pregnancy: increase dose ~30% at confirmation, target TSH <2.5. LT4/LT3 combination not routinely recommended (insufficient evidence); consider in persistently symptomatic euthyroid on LT4 alone.

name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021 + 2024 update
keys: Hour-1 bundle: lactate, blood cultures BEFORE abx, broad-spectrum within 1h, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypotension/lactate>=4, norepinephrine first-line for MAP<65 after fluids. Balanced crystalloids (SMART, BaSICS). De-escalate by 48-72h.

name: DHHS HIV ART 2024
keys: INSTI-based regimens first-line (bictegravir/TAF/FTC, dolutegravir/3TC/ABC). Long-acting cabotegravir/rilpivirine bimonthly for adherence. Earlier statin use per REPRIEVE (35% MACE reduction). Start ART regardless of CD4 count.

(3) Lung ultrasound addressed as a diagnostic modality. UNCHANGED from 2019: HCAP category eliminated, assess individual MRSA/Pseudomonas risk, CURB-65 and ATS minor criteria for site-of-care, outpatient amoxicillin or doxycycline (macrolide only if local resistance is low), inpatient beta-lactam + macrolide or respiratory fluoroquinolone.

name: IDSA/ATS HAP/VAP 2016
keys: 7-day standard duration for most HAP/VAP. Procalcitonin can guide de-escalation. Empiric coverage: anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam + MRSA coverage if risk factors. Local antibiogram-driven.

name: AHA 2023 IE Update + Duke-ISCVID
keys: Healthcare-associated IE increasing. Modified Duke-ISCVID 2023 incorporates molecular diagnostics, FDG-PET. Empiric therapy: ceftriaxone + vancomycin. POET trial: IV-to-PO transition after stabilization (>=10d IV + clinical response).

name: ATS/CDC/IDSA TB 2024
keys: 4-month rifapentine-moxifloxacin (Study 31) for drug-susceptible TB >=12 years. 6-month BPaLM (bedaquiline-pretomanid-linezolid-moxifloxacin) for RIF-resistant. LTBI: 3HP weekly x12w (preferred) or 4R.

name: IDSA/SHEA C. difficile 2021 + ACG 2024
keys: Fidaxomicin first-line over vancomycin (lower recurrence). Bezlotoxumab for high-risk recurrence prevention. FMT for >=2 recurrences. Avoid metronidazole except for fulminant CDI.

name: IDSA SSTI 2014 + 2024 updates
keys: Stratify by purulent vs nonpurulent and severity. MRSA coverage if penetrating trauma, prior MRSA, severe SIRS. Necrotizing infections: surgical debridement + broad antibiotics + clindamycin (toxin suppression). Diabetic foot: extended courses + osteomyelitis evaluation.

name: IDSA 2010/2025 UTI
keys: Uncomplicated cystitis: nitrofurantoin or TMP-SMX or fosfomycin. Complicated UTI / pyelonephritis: 5-7d fluoroquinolone (FQ) or 7-10d non-FQ. Asymptomatic bacteriuria: only treat in pregnancy or pre-urological surgery.

name: IDSA Bacterial Meningitis 2004 (still standard)
keys: Empiric: vancomycin + ceftriaxone (add ampicillin if >50yo/immunocompromised for Listeria). Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg q6h for pneumococcal (van de Beek). LP after head CT if focal deficits, papilledema, or immunocompromise.

name: IDSA Lyme 2020
keys: Doxycycline 10-14d for early erythema migrans. 14-28d for neurologic/cardiac/arthritis. Single-dose doxycycline post-tick bite if Ixodes tick + >36h attached + endemic area + <72h post-bite. No chronic Lyme syndrome.

name: ACIP Adult Immunizations 2025
keys: RZV (recombinant zoster) for all adults >=50. RSV vaccine universally for >=75; risk-based for 60-74. Pneumococcal: PCV21/PCV20/PCV15 for all >=50 (lowered from 65). Annual influenza, COVID-19, Tdap once + Td q10y.

name: IDSA Febrile Neutropenia 2024 + ASCO
keys: MASCC score risk stratification. High-risk (AML, HSCT, prolonged neutropenia >=7d): IV antipseudomonal beta-lactam + +/- vancomycin if mucositis/catheter/SSTI. Outpatient FQ for low-risk. FQ prophylaxis for high-risk.

name: WHO/IDSA Travel Medicine + Malaria
keys: Pre-travel risk assessment: destination, activities, comorbidities. Malaria chemoprophylaxis (atovaquone-proguanil, doxycycline, mefloquine, tafenoquine). Severe malaria: IV artesunate + clindamycin. Tafenoquine for P. vivax radical cure.

name: IDSA Candidiasis 2016 (still IDSA current - no update pending)
keys: NOTE: there is NO IDSA update pending - candidiasis is not on the IDSA guidelines-in-development register. A separate ECMM/ISHAM/ASM Global Guideline for Candidiasis (Lancet Infect Dis 2025) exists as a contemporary non-IDSA counterpoint but does NOT supersede IDSA 2016. Candidemia: echinocandin first-line (caspofungin 70→50 mg, micafungin 100 mg, anidulafungin 200→100 mg) — fungicidal, covers C. glabrata/krusei. Step-down to fluconazole 400 mg if susceptible + clinically stable + clearance. Remove central lines. Ophthalmology exam within 1 week (endophthalmitis). 14d from first negative blood culture. C. auris + echinocandin-resistance rising → speciation + AST mandatory. Rezafungin (once-weekly) emerging (ReSTORE).

name: ASH 2020 + 2024 VTE Treatment
keys: DOACs first-line: apixaban or rivaroxaban (no lead-in heparin); dabigatran/edoxaban require lead-in. Cancer-associated VTE: DOACs noninferior to LMWH (CARAVAGGIO, HOKUSAI-CANCER) - watch GI bleed with edoxaban. Provoked: 3 mo. Unprovoked: indefinite if low bleed risk.

name: ASH ITP 2019
keys: Steroids first-line (dexamethasone 40mg x4d preferred over prednisone). Second-line: TPO-RAs (eltrombopag, romiplostim, avatrombopag), rituximab, splenectomy. IVIG for emergent platelet rise. Fostamatinib for refractory.

name: ASH Sickle Cell 2020 + 2024
keys: Hydroxyurea standard; transfusion for stroke prevention (STOP). Voxelotor withdrawn 2024 (mortality signal); crizanlizumab disappointed in STAND. Gene therapy approved (exa-cel/CRISPR, lovo-cel) for severe SCD. Pain management with multimodal.

name: ASH TTP 2020 + HERCULES Trial
keys: Plasma exchange + caplacizumab (vWF nanobody) reduces death/recurrence/thrombosis 38%->8% (HERCULES). Steroids + rituximab for autoimmune iTTP. ADAMTS13 testing at presentation. PLASMIC score.

name: ACR/EULAR APS 2023
keys: New criteria 99% specificity. Persistent aPL (LA, aCL, anti-beta2GPI) >=12 weeks apart + clinical event. Triple-positive highest risk. Treatment: warfarin INR 2-3 (DOACs inferior per TRAPS in triple-positive); aspirin for primary prevention in obstetric APS.

name: AABB Transfusion Threshold 2023
keys: Restrictive: Hgb 7 g/dL for stable hospitalized adults (TRICC). Cardiac surgery: 7.5 g/dL. Orthopedic: 8 g/dL. Hem/onc: consider <7. Liberal in ACS uncertain (REALITY). Reduces transfusion volumes ~40%.

name: ASH 2018 Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia
keys: 4Ts score for pretest probability; low (<=3) rules out HIT, skip testing. Intermediate/high: PF4-heparin ELISA, confirm positive with serotonin release assay (SRA). Stop all heparin (including flushes) immediately; bridge with argatroban, bivalirudin, fondaparinux, or danaparoid. Avoid platelet transfusions (paradoxical thrombosis). Transition to DOAC once platelets >150k. Anticoagulate >=3 months if isolated HIT, >=3-6 months if HITT. Avoid warfarin until platelet recovery.

name: NCCN Cancer-Related Infections v3.2024 (Febrile Neutropenia)
keys: FN = ANC <500 (or <1000 with predicted nadir) + temp ≥38.3 once or ≥38.0 sustained 1h. MASCC ≥21 OR CISNE <3 = low-risk → oral cipro + amox-clav outpatient (after 2-4h observation). High-risk: IV antipseudomonal beta-lactam (cefepime, piperacillin-tazobactam, meropenem). Add vancomycin for catheter infection, mucositis, SSTI, hemodynamic instability, MRSA colonization. Empiric antifungal (echinocandin or voriconazole) after 4-7d persistent fever. FQ prophylaxis + G-CSF if expected ANC <100 >7d (AML/HSCT).

name: NCCN NSCLC v4.2024
keys: All advanced NSCLC: NGS for EGFR/ALK/ROS1/BRAF/KRAS-G12C/MET/RET/NTRK/HER2 + PD-L1 IHC. EGFR mut: osimertinib (FLAURA). ALK: alectinib/lorlatinib. KRAS-G12C: sotorasib/adagrasib (CodeBreaK 200). Adjuvant osimertinib (ADAURA), durvalumab (PACIFIC) post-CRT.

name: NCCN Breast Cancer v3.2024 + ASCO
keys: HER2+: trastuzumab + pertuzumab + taxane (CLEOPATRA); T-DXd second-line (DESTINY-Breast03). HR+: CDK4/6 inhibitors + AI/fulvestrant (PALOMA, MONALEESA, MONARCH); ribociclib OS benefit. TNBC: pembrolizumab + chemo (KEYNOTE-522). HER2-low: T-DXd.

name: NCCN Colorectal v2.2026
keys: Universal MMR/MSI testing. dMMR/MSI-H metastatic: pembrolizumab first-line (KEYNOTE-177; ORR ~30%, OS not reached). BRAF V600E: encorafenib + cetuximab/panitumumab (BEACON). Adjuvant FOLFOX/CAPOX +/- atezolizumab for stage III dMMR.

name: NCCN Prostate v5.2026
keys: Localized: surgery / radiation +/- ADT. Metastatic hormone-sensitive: ADT + docetaxel (CHAARTED) OR androgen receptor targeted (abiraterone/enzalutamide/apalutamide; LATITUDE/STAMPEDE/TITAN/ARCHES). CRPC: olaparib (BRCA, PROfound). PARPi for HRR mutations.

name: NCCN Multiple Myeloma v4.2026
keys: IMWG diagnosis: clonal plasma cells >=10% + myeloma-defining events (CRAB, biomarker SLiM-CRAB). Triplet/quadruplet induction (VRd, Dara-VRd; GRIFFIN, PERSEUS); ASCT eligibility-based. CAR-T (cilta-cel, ide-cel) for relapsed (CARTITUDE, KarMMa).

name: USPSTF Cancer Screening 2024
keys: Breast: mammography 40-74 q2y (B). Colon: 45-75 (B 45-49, A 50-75). Lung LDCT: 50-80, >=20 pack-yr, current/former (quit <15y). Cervical: HPV primary q5y 30-65 or co-test. Prostate: shared decision 55-69.

name: ASCO Immunotherapy Toxicity 2024
keys: Grade 1: continue, monitor. Grade 2: hold + consider steroids if persistent. Grade 3: hold + high-dose steroids (prednisone 1-2 mg/kg, taper 4-6 weeks). Grade 4: permanent discontinuation; immunosuppression escalation. Endocrinopathies often need lifelong replacement.

name: Cairo-Bishop TLS Definition
keys: TLS: laboratory (>=2 of K, P, uric acid, Ca within +/-25% baseline) + clinical (Cr 1.5x, arrhythmia, seizure). High risk: bulky lymphoma, AML with hyperleukocytosis, ATL. Rasburicase for high-risk; allopurinol for moderate. Aggressive IV hydration.

name: ASCO Cancer Pain 2024
keys: Multimodal pain management. Opioid titration with breakthrough doses. Adjuvants: gabapentinoids for neuropathic, dexamethasone for bone. Buprenorphine emerging for chronic cancer pain. Methadone caution (QT, drug interactions).

name: ASCO Early Breast Cancer / CDK4/6 Rapid Update 2024
keys: HR+/HER2- node-positive high-risk: adjuvant abemaciclib 150mg BID x2y + ET >=5y (monarchE: 5y IDFS absolute benefit 7.6%; Ki-67 requirement dropped 2023). Ribociclib emerging per NATALEE (stage II-III, broader population). HER2+: trastuzumab + pertuzumab + taxane (APHINITY); T-DM1 post-neoadjuvant residual (KATHERINE). Metastatic HR+: CDK4/6i + AI first-line (PALOMA-2, MONALEESA-2/7); TNBC PD-L1+ pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-355); sacituzumab govitecan (ASCENT).

name: ASCO Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Guideline 2022/2024
keys: Adjuvant stage III: FOLFOX or CAPOX x3-6mo (IDEA: 3mo non-inferior for low-risk T1-3N1). Metastatic molecular triage: RAS/BRAF/MSI/HER2 mandatory. RAS-mut or right-sided: doublet + bevacizumab (anti-VEGF). RAS-WT left-sided: doublet + cetuximab/panitumumab (anti-EGFR; PARADIGM, CALGB 80405). BRAF V600E: encorafenib + cetuximab (BEACON). dMMR/MSI-H: pembrolizumab first-line (KEYNOTE-177). Fit selected: FOLFOXIRI + bev (TRIBE).

name: ASCO/SITC Immune-Related Adverse Events 2021 (updated 2024)
keys: CTCAE v5 grading. Grade 1: continue ICI + monitor. Grade 2: hold ICI, prednisone 0.5-1 mg/kg. Grade 3-4: hold/discontinue, methylprednisolone 1-2 mg/kg + taper >=4-6wk. Steroid-refractory >48-72h: colitis → infliximab 5 mg/kg or vedolizumab 300 mg (wk 0/2/6); pneumonitis → infliximab or MMF; hepatitis → MMF (avoid infliximab); myocarditis → pulse methylpred 1g + ATG/abatacept (high mortality). Hypophysitis: hydrocortisone replacement, do NOT permanently stop ICI.

name: ASCO 2024 Stage IV NSCLC Living Guideline
keys: Universal molecular testing for EGFR/ALK/ROS1/BRAF/KRAS G12C/MET/RET/NTRK/HER2 before first-line therapy. Adjuvant osimertinib x3yr for resected EGFR+ stage IB-IIIA (ADAURA, 73% DFS benefit). Durvalumab x1yr post-concurrent CRT in unresectable stage III (PACIFIC). Metastatic non-driver: pembrolizumab monotherapy if PD-L1 >=50% (KEYNOTE-024); chemo + pembrolizumab regardless of PD-L1 (KEYNOTE-189 nonsquamous, KEYNOTE-407 squamous). Sotorasib/adagrasib for KRAS G12C post-progression (CodeBreaK 200).

name: ASCO 2025 mCRPC Living Guideline
keys: Continue ADT lifelong; layer abiraterone + prednisone or enzalutamide first-line for mCRPC (COU-AA-301, AFFIRM, PREVAIL). nmCRPC with PSADT <=10mo: apalutamide (SPARTAN), enzalutamide (PROSPER), or darolutamide (ARAMIS) added to ADT. HRR testing universal; olaparib for BRCA1/2 (PROfound) or olaparib+abiraterone (PROpel). PSMA-PET-positive post-taxane/ARPI: 177Lu-PSMA-617 (VISION, 4mo OS gain). Docetaxel then cabazitaxel (CARD) for taxane sequencing.

name: ASCO 2020 Antiemetics Guideline Update
keys: Highly emetogenic chemo (cisplatin, AC): 4-drug day 1 = NK1 RA (aprepitant/fosaprepitant/netupitant/rolapitant) + 5HT3 RA (palonosetron preferred) + dexamethasone + olanzapine 5-10mg; continue dex + olanzapine days 2-4. Moderately emetogenic: 5HT3 + dex +/- NK1. Olanzapine 5mg non-inferior to 10mg, less sedation. Olanzapine rescue for breakthrough. Same 4-drug for high-dose chemo + HSCT.

name: ASCO WBC Growth Factors 2025 Update
keys: Primary G-CSF prophylaxis (filgrastim, pegfilgrastim, tbo-filgrastim, biosimilars) when regimen-related febrile neutropenia risk >=20%, or 10-20% with patient risk factors (age >65, prior chemo/RT, advanced disease, comorbidity, poor PS). Secondary prophylaxis after prior FN/dose-limiting neutropenia. Therapeutic G-CSF not routine for afebrile neutropenia; consider in febrile neutropenia with high-risk features. Biosimilars equivalent.

name: ACR Gout 2020
keys: Treat-to-target uric acid <6 mg/dL (or <5 if tophi). Allopurinol first-line, start during flare with anti-inflammatory prophylaxis (3-6 mo). HLA-B*5801 screen in Asian populations (SCAR risk). Acute: NSAID, colchicine, OR steroid (combine for severe). Febuxostat caution per CARES (CV mortality).

name: ACR RA 2021
keys: MTX monotherapy first-line (preferred over biologics in DMARD-naive). If inadequate response: add bDMARD (anti-TNF, anti-IL6, abatacept) OR JAKi (caution >65/CV risk per ORAL Surveillance). Triple therapy (MTX/HCQ/SSZ) acceptable alternative to biologics.

name: EULAR SLE 2023
keys: Hydroxychloroquine for ALL SLE patients. Lupus nephritis: MMF + steroids; add belimumab (BLISS-LN) or voclosporin (AURORA-1) for high proteinuria. Anifrolumab (TULIP) for skin/joint disease. Goal: lupus-related damage prevention via low-dose steroids + tight DMARD control.

name: ACR ANCA Vasculitis 2021
keys: Severe GPA/MPA induction: rituximab (RAVE) preferred over cyclophosphamide; reduced-dose steroids (PEXIVAS, NNT 11). Avacopan (C5a inhibitor) steroid-sparing (ADVOCATE). Maintenance: rituximab > AZA. Plasma exchange controversial post-PEXIVAS.

name: ACR GCA 2021
keys: High-dose prednisone immediately for vision threat (1mg/kg or 1g IV pulse if vision loss). Add tocilizumab for newly-dx (GiACTA) - reduces relapse / steroid burden. Methotrexate alternative. Temporal artery biopsy + LV vascular imaging (PET, MRA). Monitor with ESR/CRP.

name: ACR/SAA/SPARTAN Axial SpA 2026
keys: 2026 update REPLACES 2019 (a first-ever juvenile axSpA companion guideline was released alongside it). NSAIDs remain first-line. MAJOR CHANGE: TNF inhibitors and IL-17 inhibitors are now EQUALLY recommended as the initial biologic - the 2019 guideline preferred TNFi first. JAK INHIBITORS are now recommended, though NOT as first-line b/tsDMARD (they were not an option in 2019). A b/tsDMARD may be initial therapy in patients with risk of progression or inadequate NSAID response. On failure, SWITCH MECHANISM OF ACTION; after two or more class failures reassess for adherence and non-inflammatory pain. Extra-musculoskeletal manifestations drive selection: uveitis or IBD -> monoclonal anti-TNF; psoriasis -> IL-17i. Well-controlled disease: gradual dose reduction may be considered, but abrupt discontinuation is recommended AGAINST. Diagnosis in adults: SI joint radiographs first, then MRI. Treat-to-target with ASDAS or BASDAI.

name: GRAPPA PsA 2022
keys: Domain-based: peripheral arthritis, axial, enthesitis, dactylitis, skin, nails. csDMARD (MTX/SSZ/LEF) vs bDMARD (TNFi, IL-17i, IL-23i, JAKi, abatacept) by domain. Treat-to-target. IL-17i (secukinumab, ixekizumab) - excellent skin + joint.

name: ACR/EULAR Sjögren 2023
keys: Sicca symptoms: artificial tears, saliva substitutes, pilocarpine, cevimeline. Systemic: hydroxychloroquine first-line; immunosuppressants (MTX, AZA, MMF) for organ involvement. Rituximab/abatacept for refractory; CD4+/CD20+ targeted therapy emerging.

name: EULAR Systemic Sclerosis 2023
keys: Skin: MMF or MTX. SSc-ILD: MMF, nintedanib (SENSCIS), tocilizumab (focuSSced). PAH: ERA + PDE5i (AMBITION). Renal crisis: ACEi (DO NOT use in pre-crisis prevention). Raynaud: CCB + PDE5i.

name: ACR Osteoarthritis 2019
keys: Exercise + weight loss core. Topical NSAIDs strongly recommended for hand/knee OA. Oral NSAIDs > acetaminophen (limited efficacy). Intra-articular steroids for flares (3-4x/year max). Avoid glucosamine/chondroitin, PRP, stem cells (insufficient evidence). Joint replacement for end-stage.

name: ACR 2025 SLE Treatment Guideline
keys: Hydroxychloroquine for ALL (target weight-based ≤5 mg/kg, retinal screen q1y after 5y). Organ-domain framework. Lupus nephritis Class III/IV: MMF + steroids + belimumab (BLISS-LN) OR voclosporin (AURORA-1, calcineurin inhibitor) triple therapy preferred over MMF alone. Non-renal SLE: anifrolumab (anti-IFNAR, TULIP-1/2) for cutaneous/articular. Steroid taper to ≤5 mg prednisone by 6 mo. Aspirin + statin + bone/vaccine/reproductive planning integrated. Belimumab maintenance reduces flares (BLISS-52/76).

name: EULAR 2022 / KDIGO 2024 ANCA-Associated Vasculitis
keys: GPA/MPA induction: rituximab (RAVE, RITUXVAS) preferred over cyclophosphamide for severe disease; both paired with PEXIVAS reduced-dose glucocorticoid taper (40% less cumulative steroid, non-inferior outcomes). Avacopan (oral C5a receptor inhibitor) added per ADVOCATE for steroid-sparing remission (week-52 superiority, cumulative prednisone -2.3g). Maintenance: rituximab 500mg q6mo > azathioprine (MAINRITSAN). EGPA severe: mepolizumab (MIRRA) or rituximab; cyclophosphamide if cardiac involvement.

name: EULAR 2022 Giant Cell Arteritis (2023 imaging update)
keys: Induction: prednisone 40-60mg/day, taper to 15-20mg by 2-3mo, off by 12mo. Tocilizumab 162mg SC weekly (GiACTA) for relapsing/refractory disease or high steroid-toxicity risk; methotrexate alternative adjunct. Diagnosis: temporal artery biopsy or temporal/axillary ultrasound (halo sign, compression sign) within 1 week; do not delay steroids. Large-vessel involvement: PET-CT, MRA, or CTA aorta. Aspirin only if ischemic/cardiovascular indication.

name: ASAS-EULAR 2022 / ACR 2019 Axial Spondyloarthritis
keys: NSAIDs first-line continuous dosing for active disease (naproxen, celecoxib); physiotherapy adjunct. Inadequate NSAID response after 2 trials: TNFi (adalimumab, infliximab, certolizumab, etanercept, golimumab) or IL-17i (secukinumab, ixekizumab, bimekizumab) without prioritization. JAKi (upadacitinib, tofacitinib) reserved for bDMARD-contraindicated/failed (per JAK safety signals, ORAL Surveillance). Imaging: MRI SI joints (bone marrow edema) for non-radiographic; pelvic X-ray for radiographic (modified NY criteria).

name: AHA/ASA Acute Ischemic Stroke 2019/2024
keys: IV alteplase (0.9 mg/kg) OR tenecteplase (0.25 mg/kg) within 4.5h LKW (extended to 9h with penumbra imaging per WAKE-UP/EXTEND/AcT). Mechanical thrombectomy <=24h for LVO with favorable imaging (DAWN, DEFUSE 3). BP <185/110 for tPA, <180/105 post-tPA.

name: AHA/ASA Stroke Prevention 2021
keys: DAPT (aspirin + clopidogrel) <=21d for minor stroke/TIA (CHANCE/POINT, start <=24h). Ticagrelor + aspirin (THALES) alternative. Statin, ACEi/ARB. AF: DOAC. Carotid stenosis 70-99% symptomatic: CEA/CAS within 2 weeks.

name: AHA/ASA ICH 2022
keys: BP control <140 within 1-2h (INTERACT2/ATACH-2). Reverse anticoagulation (4F-PCC, idarucizumab for dabigatran, andexanet for FXa). Avoid prophylactic steroids. Surgical evacuation for cerebellar ICH >3cm or hydrocephalus.

name: AAN/AES Status Epilepticus 2016 + 2024
keys: First-line benzodiazepine: IM midazolam 10mg, IV lorazepam 4mg, or IV diazepam 10mg. Second-line: fosphenytoin 20 mg/kg, valproate 40 mg/kg, levetiracetam 60 mg/kg - equivalent (ESETT). Refractory: anesthetic infusion (midazolam/propofol/pentobarbital).

name: AHS Migraine 2024
keys: Acute: triptans (sumatriptan, eletriptan), gepants (rimegepant, ubrogepant), ditans (lasmiditan), NSAIDs. Preventive: CGRP mAbs (erenumab, fremanezumab, galcanezumab, eptinezumab) FIRST-LINE (no prior trial requirement); atogepant; topiramate, propranolol. Triptans cardiac contraindications.

name: AAN/AAOS Anti-Amyloid Therapy 2024
keys: Lecanemab (CLARITY-AD: 27% slower decline) and donanemab (TRAILBLAZER-ALZ-2: 35% slower decline at low/intermediate tau) for early symptomatic AD. Eligibility: MCI/mild dementia + amyloid PET/CSF+ + APOE4 testing for ARIA risk. ARIA-E/H 20-30% (often asymptomatic).

name: International Consensus Myasthenia Gravis 2023
keys: Pyridostigmine symptomatic. Steroids + steroid-sparing (AZA, MMF, MTX). Refractory: rituximab (off-label, especially MuSK+), eculizumab/ravulizumab (C5 inhibitors), efgartigimod (FcRn antagonist per ADAPT). Thymectomy for AChR+ early-onset (MGTX).

name: EAN/PNS Guillain-Barré 2023
keys: PE OR IVIG 0.4 g/kg x5d - equally effective for hastening recovery (no advantage of combination). Steroids NOT recommended (no benefit). EGOS/mEGOS/mEGRIS prognostication. Mechanical ventilation for FVC <20 mL/kg or NIF <-30.

name: AAN Parkinson Disease 2018 + 2021 update
keys: Levodopa superior for motor (LEAP); dopamine agonists increase impulse control disorders, hallucinations, edema. MAO-B inhibitors (rasagiline, selegiline) modest. DBS for motor fluctuations / dyskinesias (EARLYSTIM). LCIG infusion for advanced disease.

name: AAN BPPV 2023
keys: Dix-Hallpike for posterior canal BPPV (most common). Torsional/upbeat nystagmus, latency 5-20s, fatigable. Treatment: Epley canalith repositioning maneuver (NNT 2). Brandt-Daroff exercises home alternative.

name: AAN 2018 (reaffirmed 2024) DMT for Adults with MS
keys: Offer DMT for relapsing MS; earlier = better long-term disability outcome. High-efficacy agents (natalizumab, ocrelizumab, alemtuzumab, ofatumumab, S1P modulators fingolimod/ozanimod) for highly active disease (TREAT-MS, DELIVER-MS support early high-efficacy). Ocrelizumab only DMT proven for ambulatory PPMS (ORATORIO). Monitor JCV antibody for natalizumab (PML risk). Switch for breakthrough activity. Pregnancy planning: glatiramer/IFN-β safest; washout for teratogenic agents.

name: AHA/ASA 2021 Secondary Stroke Prevention
keys: Etiologic workup within 48h. Non-cardioembolic minor stroke/high-risk TIA (ABCD2 >=4): DAPT aspirin + clopidogrel x21d (CHANCE, POINT) or +ticagrelor x30d (THALES). AF: DOAC over warfarin (apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, edoxaban). High-intensity statin targeting LDL <70 (SPARCL, TST). BP <130/80. PFO closure for cryptogenic stroke age <60 with high-risk PFO (CLOSE, REDUCE, RESPECT, DEFENSE-PFO). Symptomatic intracranial stenosis: aggressive medical (SAMMPRIS).

name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021/2024
keys: Hour-1 bundle. 30 mL/kg crystalloid (balanced > saline per SMART/BaSICS). Norepinephrine first-line; vasopressin add-on. Hydrocortisone 200 mg/day for refractory shock (ADRENAL/APROCCHSS). Lactate-guided resuscitation.

name: ATS/ESICM ARDS 2023
keys: Low TV 4-8 mL/kg PBW. Plateau pressure <30. Prone position >=16h/day for moderate-severe (PROSEVA, NNT 6). NMB for refractory P/F<150 (ROSE). VV-ECMO referral for refractory (CESAR, EOLIA).

name: ICU Liberation (Pain/Sedation/Delirium) 2018/2024
keys: ABCDEF bundle: Assess pain, Both SAT/SBT, Choice of sedation, Delirium monitor, Early mobility, Family. Avoid benzos (preferred propofol/dexmedetomidine). Reduces ICU LOS, mortality, delirium.

name: AAAAI/ACAAI Anaphylaxis 2023
keys: IM epinephrine 0.3-0.5 mg first-line (lateral thigh). Biphasic reactions 5-20% within 24h - observation 4-8h. Antihistamines/steroids ADJUNCTS only. Self-injectable epinephrine + 911 activation for at-risk patients.

name: GINA Asthma 2024
keys: Track 1 preferred: ICS-formoterol PRN (mild) up to scheduled+PRN reliever (severe). Track 2: SABA + ICS. Type-2 biologics (omalizumab, mepolizumab/reslizumab/benralizumab anti-IL-5, dupilumab anti-IL-4Ra, tezepelumab anti-TSLP) for severe.

name: AAAAI/ACAAI Drug Allergy 2022
keys: Direct oral challenge for low-risk penicillin allergy (95% delabeling). Skin testing for high-risk. Graded challenges for radiocontrast/sulfonamides/NSAIDs. Avoid empiric desensitization without confirmed allergy.

name: HAEA/WAO Hereditary Angioedema 2021
keys: On-demand: C1-INH concentrate, ecallantide, icatibant. Long-term prophylaxis: lanadelumab (FcRn anti-pKLK; reduces attacks 86%, HELP), berotralstat (oral pKLK inhibitor), C1-INH SC. Self-administer all therapies.

name: AAAAI Food Allergy / OIT 2024
keys: Strict avoidance + epinephrine for risk-management. Palforzia (peanut OIT) FDA-approved ages 1-17 (POSEIDON, PALISADE). Omalizumab 2024 FDA approval reduces severe reactions in multi-food allergy (OUtMATCH). SLIT/EPIT emerging.

name: AAAAI Allergic Rhinitis 2017/2023
keys: INCS first-line monotherapy. INCS + intranasal antihistamine combination effective. Oral 2nd-gen antihistamines safer than 1st-gen. SCIT/SLIT for refractory/IgE-mediated. Avoid depot steroids.

name: AAAAI/ACAAI Drug Allergy Practice Parameter 2022
keys: Penicillin allergy delabeling priority — 95% of labeled patients tolerate penicillin; label associated with broader antibiotic use, MRSA/C. difficile, longer admissions. Risk-stratify by history: low-risk (isolated GI symptoms, remote benign rash, family-only history, unknown reaction >10y) eligible for direct oral amoxicillin challenge without skin testing. Moderate-risk (urticaria, pruritus): penicillin skin testing then graded challenge. High-risk (anaphylaxis, SJS/TEN, DRESS): avoid. Sulfonamide antibiotic-to-non-antibiotic cross-reactivity is a myth — sulfasalazine, diuretics, celecoxib safe. RCM premed with prednisone + diphenhydramine.

name: AAD/NPF Psoriasis 2019 + 2024 biologics update
keys: Anti-IL-23 (guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab) and anti-IL-17 (secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab, bimekizumab) preferred for moderate-severe. Anti-TNF (adalimumab, etanercept, infliximab) alternative. IL-23i favor less frequent dosing, lower candidiasis.

name: AAD Atopic Dermatitis 2024
keys: Topical steroids + emollients + barrier care first-line. Topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) for face/folds. Severe: dupilumab (anti-IL-4Ra), tralokinumab (anti-IL-13), abrocitinib/baricitinib/upadacitinib (JAKi). Topical ruxolitinib for mild-moderate.

name: AAD Acne 2024
keys: Strong recommendations: BPO, topical retinoids (tretinoin, adapalene, tazarotene), topical/oral antibiotics (limited duration), oral spironolactone (women), combined oral contraceptives. Isotretinoin for severe/scarring (iPLEDGE).

name: USPSTF Skin Cancer Screening 2023
keys: Insufficient evidence for routine visual skin screening in asymptomatic adults (I statement). Does not apply to symptomatic, high-risk (immunocompromised, prior cancer, family history, dysplastic nevi). AAD continues to recommend self-exams + dermatologist evaluation.

name: IDSA SSTI / Cellulitis 2014/2024
keys: Nonpurulent cellulitis: oral cephalexin or amoxicillin (Strep coverage). Purulent: incision + drainage; add MRSA coverage (TMP-SMX, doxycycline, clindamycin) if SIRS. Severe: IV vancomycin/daptomycin/linezolid. Diabetic foot: extended courses, image for osteomyelitis.

name: AAD/HSF Hidradenitis Suppurativa 2019/2024
keys: Adalimumab (anti-TNF) FDA-approved (PIONEER 1/2; HiSCR 40-59%). Secukinumab (anti-IL-17A; SUNRISE/SUNSHINE) approved 2023. Bimekizumab approved 2024. Surgical excision for fibrotic stages.

name: AAD-NPF 2020/2021 Psoriasis (Topicals + Biologics)
keys: Topical corticosteroids + vitamin D analogs (calcipotriene) first-line for limited disease; phototherapy (NB-UVB) for moderate. Biologics for moderate-severe: TNFi (etanercept, adalimumab, infliximab), IL-17i (secukinumab, ixekizumab, brodalumab), IL-23i (guselkumab, risankizumab, tildrakizumab). Oral: apremilast, methotrexate, cyclosporine, acitretin, deucravacitinib. Screen all for psoriatic arthritis and cardiometabolic comorbidities.

name: AAD 2023/2024 Atopic Dermatitis
keys: Emollients + bathing, topical corticosteroids first-line; topical calcineurin inhibitors (tacrolimus, pimecrolimus) and crisaborole for face/folds/steroid-sparing; topical ruxolitinib for mild-moderate. NB-UVB phototherapy for refractory. Strong recommendations for dupilumab (anti-IL-4Ra, LIBERTY-AD), tralokinumab (anti-IL-13, ECZTRA), and oral JAKi abrocitinib/upadacitinib/baricitinib (JADE, Measure Up, BREEZE-AD) for moderate-severe.

name: APA Major Depression 2024 + ACP 2023
keys: First-line: SSRIs (sertraline, escitalopram), SNRIs, mirtazapine, bupropion. Treatment-resistant (>=2 failed): augmentation (lithium, T3, atypical antipsychotic) OR ketamine/esketamine (NMDA antagonist; STAR*D, TRD-IV). ECT for severe / refractory. CBT/IPT comparable to medication for mild-moderate.

name: APA/WFSBP Bipolar Disorder
keys: Acute mania: lithium, valproate, atypical antipsychotics. Bipolar depression: lithium or lamotrigine (NOT antidepressant monotherapy - switch risk). Maintenance: lithium gold standard (suicide prevention). Avoid valproate in reproductive-age women (teratogenicity, MHRA).

name: APA PTSD 2023
keys: First-line: trauma-focused CBT (CPT, PE, EMDR) + SSRI/SNRI (sertraline, paroxetine, venlafaxine FDA-approved). Prazosin for nightmares. Avoid benzos. MDMA-assisted therapy under FDA review (denied 2024 - additional evidence required).

name: APA Schizophrenia 2020/2024
keys: Atypical antipsychotic first-line (avoid first-gen unless clozapine intolerance). Clozapine for treatment-resistant (>=2 failed) - reduces suicide. LAI antipsychotics for adherence (1-3 month formulations). Cognitive behavioral therapy + supported employment.

name: SAMHSA TIP 63 / ASAM OUD
keys: MAT first-line: buprenorphine (mu partial agonist; office-based; X-waiver removed 2023), methadone (opioid agonist; OTP only), naltrexone (mu antagonist; XR-NTX preferred). Concurrent psychosocial. Naloxone co-prescription for overdose risk.

name: APA Eating Disorders 2023
keys: First major update since 2006. Anorexia: weight restoration + family-based therapy (adolescents) or eating-disorder-focused CBT (adults). Bulimia/BED: CBT-ED + SSRI (fluoxetine 60mg). Lisdexamfetamine for BED. Olanzapine for severe AN weight gain.

name: AASM Insomnia 2017/2024
keys: CBT-I FIRST-line (digital CBT-I expanded access). Pharmacotherapy: dual orexin antagonists (suvorexant, lemborexant, daridorexant) preferred over benzos/Z-drugs. Melatonin/ramelteon for circadian. Avoid chronic benzo/Z-drug use.

name: AGS/BGS/WFG Falls Prevention 2022 (World Falls Guidelines)
keys: Multifactorial assessment: vision, gait, cognition, medications (esp. anticholinergics, benzos, sleep aids per Beers), home hazards. Exercise + balance training (tai chi). Vitamin D if deficient. STOPPFall medication review. Screen all >=65 annually with Timed Up-and-Go.

name: AGS Beers Criteria 2023
keys: Potentially inappropriate medications in >=65: anticholinergics (cumulative burden -> falls/dementia), benzos (falls, delirium), NSAIDs (GI/renal/CV), tertiary TCAs, glyburide, megestrol, PPI >8 weeks. Drug-disease and drug-drug warnings. Cumulative anticholinergic score added 2023.

name: NPIAP/EPUAP/PPPIA Pressure Injury 2025 (4th ed, living guideline)
keys: 4th edition (2025) SUPERSEDES the 2019 static document and is a LIVING guideline with staged chapter release (prevention chapters live from Feb 2025). Framework unchanged: stages 1-4 plus unstageable and deep tissue injury; risk assessment (Braden, Norton); repositioning, support surfaces, nutritional support; staging guides treatment - stage 1 protect, stage 2 hydrocolloid or foam, stages 3-4 debridement, negative-pressure wound therapy, consider surgery. CAUTION: specific numeric recommendations from 2019 (repositioning interval, support-surface selection, nutrition targets) are being revised chapter by chapter - verify against the current chapter before teaching a specific threshold.

name: AAOS Hip Fracture 2021
keys: Surgery within 24-48h reduces mortality. Geriatric co-management (NICE/HELLP). Regional anesthesia (fascia iliaca block) for analgesia. Pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis. Bisphosphonate / denosumab for osteoporosis after.

name: Frailty assessment - Fried phenotype and Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale
keys: CAUTION - this entry is a synthesis of the standard frailty instruments, NOT a named AGS practice guideline; do not cite it as an AGS guideline. Phenotypic model (Fried 5 criteria): unintentional weight loss, weakness, exhaustion, slow gait speed, low physical activity - 3 or more equals frail. Deficit-accumulation model: Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale / Frailty Index. Frailty predicts increased surgical and hospital risk; optimize before elective surgery. NOTE: the instruments are known to be DISCORDANT with one another, and JAGS 2026 proposes a Frailty Trajectory Model subtyping frailty by driver and expected treatment response.

name: AAHPM End-of-Life 2024
keys: Goals-of-care discussions early (ask-tell-ask). Hospice eligibility: prognosis <=6 months. POLST/MOLST documentation across settings. Symptom management hierarchy: pain (opioid titration, adjuvants), dyspnea (opioids), delirium (haloperidol).

name: ACOG Breast Cancer Screening 2024
keys: Begin annual or biennial mammography at age 40 for average-risk (USPSTF 40-74 q2y; ACS 45-54 annually then biennial). Risk assessment for BRCA / family history -> earlier MRI screening. Stop ~age 75 individualized.

name: USPSTF Cervical Cancer Screening 2023
keys: Ages 21-29: Pap q3y. Ages 30-65: HPV primary q5y (preferred), co-testing q5y, OR Pap q3y. Stop at 65 if adequate screening and no high-grade lesions in 25 years. ACS 2025 update: start age 25, HPV primary preferred (incl. self-collection).

name: CDC US MEC Contraception 2024
keys: Categories 1 (no restriction) - 4 (unacceptable). LARC (IUD, implant) most effective; encourage as first-line. CHCs contraindicated in: smokers >=35, migraine with aura, breast cancer, severe HTN, VTE history. Updated for CKD, postpartum, transplant.

name: NAMS Menopause Hormone Therapy 2022
keys: HT most effective for VMS. Favorable benefit-risk for symptomatic women <60 OR <10 years from menopause onset. Transdermal estrogen LOWER VTE/stroke risk vs oral. Add progestogen if uterus present. Bazedoxifene/CEE (Duavee) alternative.

name: ACOG Hypertension in Pregnancy 2024
keys: Severe features: SBP>=160, DBP>=110, plt<100k, AST/ALT 2x normal, Cr>1.1, pulmonary edema, neuro symptoms. Aspirin 81mg from 12-28 weeks if high-risk preeclampsia. Mag sulfate for severe features / eclampsia. Deliver 37w (no severe) or 34w (severe).

name: ACOG Endometriosis 2026
keys: Clinical diagnosis with empiric medical therapy (NSAIDs, CHCs, progestins, GnRH agonists/antagonists, elagolix). TVUS first imaging (deep infiltrating disease). Laparoscopy not required for diagnosis. Avoid biomarker testing.

name: ACOG Gestational Diabetes 2024 (CPG #2)
keys: Universal 2-step screen at 24-28 wk: 50g GCT → 100g 3h OGTT if abnormal; Carpenter-Coustan criteria (2 of 4 abnormal). Early screening if BMI ≥25 (≥23 Asian) + risk factors (A1c ≥5.7, prior GDM, PCOS). Lifestyle first; insulin preferred if pharmacologic needed (metformin/glyburide cross placenta, second-line). Targets: fasting <95, 1h pp <140, 2h pp <120. Delivery 39-40w (A1), 39w (A2 controlled). Postpartum 75g OGTT 4-12 wk; 50-70% lifetime T2DM risk.

name: NAMS 2020 Genitourinary Syndrome of Menopause Position Statement
keys: Non-hormonal lubricants/long-acting moisturizers first for mild symptoms. Low-dose vaginal estrogen (cream, tablet, ring) first-line prescription for moderate-severe GSM; minimal systemic absorption, endometrial protection generally not required. Vaginal DHEA (prasterone) and oral ospemifene (SERM) effective alternatives. Systemic ET if vasomotor symptoms coexist. Energy-based therapies (CO2 laser, RF) insufficient evidence; not recommended outside trials.

name: ACOG 2022 Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (Practice Bulletin 194 update)
keys: Rotterdam criteria: 2 of 3 (oligo-/anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, polycystic ovarian morphology on US) after exclusion of CAH, Cushing, thyroid, prolactinoma. Screen all for T2DM (2-hr 75g OGTT), dyslipidemia, OSA, endometrial cancer risk. Combined OCs first-line for menstrual regulation/hirsutism; spironolactone adjunct. Metformin for metabolic/glycemic. Letrozole first-line for ovulation induction (PPCOS II: higher live births vs clomiphene). GLP-1 RA emerging for weight.

name: AAO Diabetic Retinopathy PPP 2024
keys: Annual dilated exams: T1DM start 5y after onset; T2DM at diagnosis. Anti-VEGF (aflibercept, ranibizumab, bevacizumab, faricimab) first-line for center-involved DME. PRP for proliferative DR. Tighter glycemic + BP control slow progression (DCCT, UKPDS).

name: AAO Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma 2025
keys: Latanoprost or other PG analog first-line (UKGTS: -3.8 mmHg, slows VF progression). Add second/third agents to reach target IOP 25-30% reduction. SLT (selective laser trabeculoplasty) per LiGHT trial - first-line alternative. MIGS for moderate disease.

name: AAO Age-Related Macular Degeneration 2024
keys: Wet AMD: anti-VEGF (aflibercept, faricimab, ranibizumab, brolucizumab) monthly initially, then treat-and-extend or PRN. Dry AMD: AREDS2 (lutein/zeaxanthin/zinc/Cu/vit C/E) slows progression 25% (no benefit if smoker for AREDS). Geographic atrophy: pegcetacoplan/avacincaptad pegol new.

name: ACR/EULAR GCA 2021 (Vision Loss Lens)
keys: Sudden vision loss: IV methylprednisolone 1g x 3d -> oral pred 1mg/kg taper. Add tocilizumab (GiACTA: 56% sustained remission vs 14% with steroids alone). Temporal artery biopsy + LV imaging. ESR + CRP + IL-6 monitoring.

name: AAN/AAO Optic Neuritis (ONTT)
keys: ONTT: IV methylprednisolone 1g/d x 3d + oral pred speeds visual recovery (~2 wks vs ~5 wks placebo). Oral pred ALONE inferior - increases recurrence. No long-term VA benefit. MRI predicts MS conversion (15-yr: 50% if abnormal vs 22% if normal).

name: AAO-HNS Acute Rhinosinusitis 2025
keys: Watchful waiting OR amoxicillin-clavulanate 5-7d for uncomplicated ABRS. Watchful waiting if reliable follow-up. Antibiotic if symptoms >=10d or worsening or severe (T>39, facial pain). Imaging only if complications (orbital/intracranial).

name: AAP/AAFP Acute Otitis Media 2013
keys: Diagnose with TM bulging or fluid + recent symptoms. Severe: T>=39 or moderate-severe otalgia or >=48h symptoms = antibiotics. Mild + reliable follow-up = watchful waiting. Amoxicillin 80-90 mg/kg/day; amoxicillin-clavulanate if treatment failure / recent ATB.

name: IDSA Group A Strep Pharyngitis 2025 (Part 1: testing) + 2012 (treatment)
keys: TESTING - 2025 Part 1 (Oct 2025) CHANGES PRACTICE: clinical scoring systems (Centor/McIsaac, FeverPAIN) now explicitly gate WHETHER TO TEST AT ALL - do NOT test and do not treat low-risk patients. This reverses the 2012 posture of near-universal RADT or culture in adults with pharyngitis. TREATMENT - Part 2 (treatment, duration, penicillin allergy) is still PENDING (estimated late 2026), so 2012 treatment guidance still stands: penicillin V or amoxicillin first-line for 10 days; cephalosporin, clindamycin, or azithromycin if penicillin-allergic; no test of cure after RADT in adults.

name: AAN Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo 2023
keys: Most common cause peripheral vertigo. Dix-Hallpike test for posterior canal: torsional/upbeat nystagmus, latency 5-20s, fatigable, resolves <60s. Epley canalith repositioning maneuver (NNT 2). Brandt-Daroff exercises home alternative.

name: AAO-HNS Sudden SNHL 2019
keys: Idiopathic SNHL: high-dose oral steroids within 2 weeks (prednisone 1 mg/kg x 7-14d). Intratympanic dexamethasone if oral failure / contraindication. Hyperbaric O2 + steroids for salvage <1 mo. MRI to rule out vestibular schwannoma.

name: AAO-HNS Hoarseness 2018
keys: Laryngoscopy if dysphonia >4 weeks or earlier with red flags (smoker, hemoptysis, neck mass, dysphagia). Avoid empiric PPI for non-LPR symptoms. Voice therapy for muscle tension dysphonia.

name: AHRQ Quality Indicators (PSI/IQI/PQI)
keys: Patient Safety Indicators (PSI): hospital-acquired adverse events. Inpatient Quality Indicators (IQI): mortality, utilization. Prevention Quality Indicators (PQI): ambulatory-care-sensitive admissions. Used for hospital comparison and CMS pay-for-performance.

name: IHI Quintuple Aim 2022
keys: The QUINTUPLE AIM is IHI current and supersedes the Triple Aim for teaching. Evolution: TRIPLE Aim (IHI 2008 - improve population health, improve patient experience, reduce per-capita cost) -> QUADRUPLE Aim (Bodenheimer and Sinsky 2014 - adds clinician well-being) -> QUINTUPLE Aim (Nundy, Cooper, Mate; IHI/JAMA 2022 - adds HEALTH EQUITY). Presenting the Triple Aim as IHI current framework is out of date.

name: IHI Model for Improvement (PDSA)
keys: Three questions: aim? measures? changes? PDSA cycles (Plan-Do-Study-Act) for iterative testing. Run charts and SPC for measurement. Integrated with Lean / Six Sigma DMAIC.

name: AMA Code of Medical Ethics 2024
keys: Four principles: autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice. Capacity (clinical, decision-specific, can fluctuate) vs competence (legal, global). Informed consent: information + voluntariness + capacity. No ethical difference between withholding/withdrawing care.

name: USPSTF Methodology + Grade Definitions
keys: Grade A (high certainty, substantial benefit): offer/provide. Grade B (moderate benefit): offer. Grade C (small benefit): selectively offer. Grade D (no benefit/harm): don't offer. Grade I (insufficient): document limitations.

name: IDSA/SHEA Antimicrobial Stewardship
keys: Core elements: leadership commitment, accountability, drug expertise. Strategies: preauthorization, prospective audit + feedback, formulary restriction. Reduces CDI 26%, costs ~$200-400K/yr/hospital. CDC Core Elements mandated by Joint Commission.

name: USPSTF Recommendations 2024
keys: A/B grade: cancer screening (mammography 40-74, colonoscopy/FIT 45-75, lung LDCT 50-80, cervical HPV 30-65). HTN screening adults. Statin 40-75 with ASCVD risk >=10%. Aspirin 40-59 with ASCVD risk >=10% individualized. AAA screening 65-75 male smokers.

name: ACIP Adult Immunizations 2025
keys: Influenza annually, COVID-19. Tdap once + Td q10y. RZV >=50, RSV >=75 (60-74 risk-based), pneumococcal PCV21/PCV20/PCV15 >=50, HPV through 45. MMR/varicella if no immunity. Travel: hepatitis A/B, typhoid, yellow fever.

name: ACC/AHA ASCVD Risk Calculator (PREVENT 2025)
keys: PREVENT replaces pooled cohort equations: more accurate across race/ethnicity. Includes kidney function (eGFR), glycemia, social determinants. 10-year + 30-year ASCVD risk. Statin shared decision >=7.5% 10-year risk.

name: USPSTF Aspirin for Primary CV Prevention 2022
keys: Initiate ASA 81 mg in 40-59 with 10-yr ASCVD risk >=10% (C grade - small benefit). Do NOT initiate >=60 (D grade - bleeding outweighs). ARRIVE/ASCEND/ASPREE shifted recommendations away from broad primary prevention.

name: USPSTF Tobacco Cessation 2021 + ATS 2020 Pharmacotherapy
keys: 5As (Ask, Advise, Assess, Assist, Arrange) all adults (A grade). Combination behavioral + pharmacotherapy most effective. ATS 2020: varenicline (nicotinic partial agonist) > NRT > bupropion (EAGLES showed no excess neuropsychiatric/CV events). Varenicline + nicotine patch superior to monotherapy. Extended duration (12→24 wk) increases abstinence. Pregnancy: behavioral only (insufficient evidence for pharmacotherapy). E-cigarettes: insufficient evidence (I statement); not first-line.

name: AAHPM Pain Management 2024
keys: Multimodal: WHO ladder (NSAIDs/acetaminophen -> weak opioids -> strong opioids). Methadone unique (NMDA antagonist + mu agonist - QT, drug interactions). Adjuvants: gabapentinoids (neuropathic), dexamethasone (bone), bisphosphonates. Opioid rotation if dose-limiting toxicity.

name: AAHPM Goals-of-Care 2024 (EPAs)
keys: Ask-tell-ask framework. Elicit values, not just preferences. Document POLST/MOLST across settings. Five wishes / advance directive components: medical decisions, person to make them, comfort, treatment, family. Code status discussion before procedures.

name: ASCO Palliative Care for Patients With Cancer 2024
keys: 2024 update REPLACES 2017. Core recommendation unchanged: refer to interdisciplinary palliative care EARLY and CONCURRENTLY with cancer therapy from diagnosis of advanced disease (TEMEL: improved QoL, mood, possibly survival). NEW IN 2024: early integration explicitly EXTENDED to patients with HEMATOLOGIC MALIGNANCIES and to patients enrolled on EARLY-PHASE CLINICAL TRIALS - both under-addressed in 2017. Explicit endorsement of TELEHEALTH-delivered palliative care, and of needs-based prioritization plus primary palliative care by the oncology team to manage capacity constraints. Hospice eligibility: prognosis of 6 months or less. Hospital-based palliative care reduces ICU days and costs.
